Author: Krishan Pahal
Bench: Krishan Pahal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:112436
Court No. - 68
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 18401 of 2024
Applicant :- Sandeep
Opposite Party :- State Of Up And 3 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Satya Priya Mishra

Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
Learned A.G.A. has informed that the notice to the informant has been served on 18.05.2024.

2. Heard Sri Mahendra Kumar Yadav, Advocate holding brief of Sri Amarendra Mani, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Satya Priya Mishra, learned counsel for the informant, Sri Pranshu Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.27 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Taryasujan, District Kushinagar, during the pendency of trial.
4. As per prosecution story, the applicant alongwith co-accused person Pankaj is stated to have enticed away the minor daughter of the informant on 17.12.2023.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The FIR is delayed by thirty four days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The applicant himself is less than 18 years old.
The victim and the applicant are almost of same age.
The victim, by her appearance, looks to be major.

Learned counsel has further stated that as per school certificate issued by principal, the date of birth of the victim is stated to be 01.01.2008, which comes out to be 15 years, 11 months and 16 days.
The said certificate issued by the principal cannot be relied as it does not fall in any category provided under Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. In support of his submission, learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance on the judgment of Supreme Court passed in P. Yuvaprakash vs State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525, wherein the Supreme Court has observed that in the absence of records relating to the birth of the victim, no other documents except the Matriculation or equivalent certificate from the concerned examination board or certificate by a corporation, municipal authority or a Panchayat can be relied upon to ascertain the age of the victim.

entities.text: P. Yuvaprakash vs State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that as per her own statement, the victim has stated her age to be 17 years.

The victim is a consenting party as is but evident from her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., whereby she has stated that she had gone with the applicant all the way to Maharashtra and had married him in a Shiva Temple.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 29.01.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicant is released on bail,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
8. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.
9. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

A person's right to life and liberty,
guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because he or she is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. has not shown any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
10. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A. for the State.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: POCSO was formulated to protect children under the age of 18 years from sexual exploitation.
Nowadays, more often than not it has become a tool for their exploitation.
The Act was never meant to criminalise consensual romantic relationships between adolescents.
However, this has to be seen from the facts and circumstances of each case.

The factum of consensual relationship borne out of love should be of consideration while granting bail because it would amount to perversity of justice if the statement of victim was ignored and accused was left to suffer behind jail.

12. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant- Sandeep, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

15. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 15.7.2024 Ravi/-
(Justice Krishan Pahal)
